back: Blood vessels with a pump (the heart) and valves that keep blood flowing in one direction.
Blood passes through the heart twice per complete circuit: pulmonary (heart–lungs) and systemic (heart–body).
Blood from the lungs is pumped again, reaching the body at high pressure, so oxygen and glucose are delivered quickly.
notes: The lungs get blood at lower pressure; oxygenated and deoxygenated blood stay separate.

front: (Supplement) Route of blood in a fish's single circulation?
back: Heart → gills → body → heart (through the heart once per circuit).

front: Path of blood through the heart?
back: Vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta.
Supply the heart muscle with oxygen and glucose; they branch from the aorta.

front: (Supplement) Why is the left ventricle wall the thickest?
back: It pumps blood at high pressure all round the body; the right ventricle pumps only to the lungs.
notes: Both ventricles pump the same volume.

front: (Supplement) Names and positions of the heart valves?
back: Atrioventricular valves (tricuspid right, bicuspid left) between atria and ventricles; semilunar valves at the bases of the aorta and pulmonary artery.

front: What causes the 'lub' and 'dub' heart sounds?
back: Lub: atrioventricular valves closing. Dub: semilunar valves closing.

front: Three ways to monitor the activity of the heart?
back: ECG (electrical activity), pulse rate, and listening to the valves with a stethoscope.

front: Why does heart rate increase during exercise?
back: Muscles respire faster, needing more oxygen and glucose and making more CO₂; faster heartbeat delivers and removes these more quickly.
